messages:
support_ella: Heads-up — we got a priority ticket from an enterprise customer. They reported a spike in 502/504s hitting hosted inference endpoints starting right after this morning's canary. Sample: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'` returned 502s repeatedly.
ops-bot: Deploy notification: canary rollout deploy-2026-03-18-08:12 started by maya. tagging: kernelpath-v2, prefetch-window=on
oncall_ryan: I'm looking at gateway graphs — 5xx rate jumped ~12:35 UTC and aligns with canary start. Error surface: gateway timeouts + upstream 502 from model pods. Rolling window: ~3-7% of traffic in canary slice.
sam: Do we have auth failures mixed in or purely backend 5xx? I see auth 401s stable. This looks like upstream service errors (502/504) — logs show `failed to deserialize request` in some pods.
maya: I pushed a config change to enable `prefetch-window` behavior in kernelpath-v2 for the canary. It was supposed to be safe. I rolled canary to 10% at 08:12, then 30% at 08:30.
leah: Confirming logs from model-runtime: `panic: kvcache: unexpected nil` appears in stack traces around the same time. A subset of canary pods hit that after first few requests.
cs_jordan: Customer reports: "Our production traffic sees intermittent 502s and timeouts; this started after you rolled something out this morning — can you advise?" They're asking for ETA and mitigation.
oncall_ryan: Okay — mitigation plan: 1) Pause rollout, 2) Lower canary traffic to 0% (drain), 3) If errors persist on remaining canary pods, rollback to previous stable image. Who can cut the percentage now?
maya: Pausing and initiating traffic drain. Running `kubectl -n inference set canary weight deploy/kernelpath-v2-canary=0` and draining active connections.
ops-bot: Canary weight update: kernelpath-v2-canary -> 0% (by maya) — traffic will shift over 30s.
sam: Repro attempt steps I used: send a short burst of 10 concurrent requests with sequence length 128 to the canary endpoint. I get 2-3 502s consistently. Example load test command: `hey -n 50 -c 10 -m POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
leah: Post-drain telemetry: 5xx rate falling but still elevated in some AZs. Seeing a class of failures with `json: invalid use of ,string struct tag` in deserializers for requests with a `max_tokens` int field — suggests a config mismatch in request shaping.
maya: Hmm — I toggled a feature flag that changes how `max_tokens` is marshaled through prefetch—looks like prefetch-window=on path expects strings. That explains the deserialization panic in some runtime versions.
sam: That would cause `panic` in older runtime builds if they hit the marshaling path. Does the canary image include the marshaling change? maya: Yes, kernelpath-v2 includes the prefetch marshaler change.
oncall_ryan: So root cause hypothesis: canary combines runtime change + config flag flip causing incompatible marshaling -> upstream panics -> gateway 502/504. Next step: full rollback of canary image + revert flag, coordinate with release window.
cs_jordan: Customer wants immediate rollback and ETA. Can we give them a timeframe?
maya: I can roll back to last stable image now. Rolling `image: registry.redwood/kernelpath:v1.14` back to deployment and will redeploy canary with previous runtime.
ops-bot: Rollout event: started rollback to registry.redwood/kernelpath:v1.14 (maya). Estimated 3m for new pods to come up.
leah: After rollback starting, I'm watching error rates. If they don't drop after pods are healthy we may need to clear in-flight caches / restart ingress proxies. I'll coordinate.
sam: Also flag state: we should set `prefetch-window=off` account-wide until we validate. maya can you flip that after rollback? Note: config propagation takes ~45s.
maya: Will flip flag to `off` in featurestore. Doing `PATCH /admin/flags/prefetch-window {"value":false}`
oncall_ryan: Post-rollback check plan: 1) confirm all canary pods are v1.14 healthy 2) validate 30m of low 5xx in dashboards 3) reopen canary at 5% with additional logging and perf gating.
cs_jordan: I'll let the customer know we're reverting and will follow up in ~10 min with status. They asked for a postmortem once fixed.
support_ella: Adding ticket notes and escalation path. Marking as P1 and notifying account execs.
maya: Rollback completed — new pods healthy at 08:48 UTC. Canary now at 0 and deployment reverted to v1.14.
leah: Early telemetry: gateway 5xx back down to baseline after a short tail. Some cached requests failed but overall good. I'll keep monitoring for 20m.
sam: Repro attempts against v1.14 returned 0/50 502s. Looks clean.
oncall_ryan: Great. Action items: - maya to open a follow-up PR to decouple marshaler change from flag gating - leah to run canary runbook with extra validations next time - sam to add automated schema validation for request shaping - support_ella to send customer update and set expectation for postmortem.
cs_jordan: Customer notified — they appreciate the quick rollback. They'll wait for postmortem.
support_ella: Closing alert for now, leaving incident channel open until 20:20 UTC for handoff.
leah: Logging follow-up: I captured podstack traces and will attach to the ticket. Root cause looks like marshaler/flag interplay causing `nil` kvcache and json unmarshal panics.
maya: Agree. Sorry team — I'll draft the PR and coordinate a controlled rollout with schema checks.
sam: Thanks everyone. I'll write up repro steps and include `hey` command and sample payloads in the bug.
support_ella: Thanks all :thumbsup
notes: incident handled: rollback performed, postmortem pending
